questions.text: A retail store advertises a 10% discount on the marked price of a television. After this discount is applied, the store offers an additional 5% off on the already reduced price. What is the overall percentage discount on the original marked price?
questions.solution:
Let the marked price be 100 units.
First discount: 10% of 100 = 10 → price = 100‑10 = 90.
Second discount: 5% of 90 = 4.5 → price = 90‑4.5 = 85.5.
Total discount = 100‑85.5 = 14.5 units.
Hence overall discount = 14.5% of the original price.

questions.text: Rahul invests ₹20,000 in a scheme offering 8% p.a. compound interest, compounded annually. At the end of the first year, the bank revises the rate to 10% p.a. for the second year. Rahul withdraws 25% of the amount (including interest) at the end of the first year and reinvests the remaining at the revised rate for the second year. What is the total amount he receives at the end of the second year?
questions.solution:
Amount after 1st year = 20000 × 1.08 = ₹21,600.
Withdrawal = 25% of 21,600 = ₹5,400.
Remaining invested = 21,600 – 5,400 = ₹16,200.
Amount after 2nd year = 16,200 × 1.10 = ₹17,820.
Total received = Withdrawal + Final amount = 5,400 + 17,820 = ₹23,220.

questions.text: A tea vendor mixes 3 kg of Type A tea costing Rs 120 per kg with 2 kg of Type B tea costing Rs 150 per kg. He sells half of this mixture at a 10 % profit on its cost. He then adds 1 kg of Type C tea costing Rs 180 per kg to the remaining mixture and sells the rest at the same selling price per kg as used for the first half. What is the overall profit percentage on the whole transaction (rounded to two decimal places)?
questions.solution:
1. Initial cost =3×120+2×150=660 Rs; total qty=5 kg; cost/kg=660/5=132 Rs.
2. 10 % profit ⇒ selling price/kg for first half =132×1.10=145.2 Rs.
3. Revenue from first half (2.5 kg)=2.5×145.2=363 Rs.
4. Cost of remaining 2.5 kg =2.5×132=330 Rs.
5. Add Type C: extra cost=1×180=180 Rs; new total cost=330+180=510 Rs; new qty=3.5 kg.
6. Selling price per kg for second part is same as step 2 =145.2 Rs.
7. Revenue from second part=3.5×145.2=508.2 Rs.
8. Total revenue=363+508.2=871.2 Rs; total cost=660+180=840 Rs; profit=31.2 Rs.
9. Overall profit % = (31.2/840)×100≈3.71 %

questions.text: A continuous random variable X has a probability density function f(x) = kx² for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2 and 0 otherwise. Find the value of k and calculate P(X > 1).
questions.solution: For f(x) to be a valid PDF, the integral from 0 to 2 of kx² dx must equal 1. ∫₀² kx² dx = [kx³/3]₀² = 8k/3 = 1 => k = 3/8. Then P(X > 1) = ∫₁² (3/8)x² dx = (3/8)[x³/3]₁² = (1/8)(8 - 1) = 7/8. Option B has the wrong k, Option C has both wrong, and Option D has the correct k but wrong probability.

questions.text: A suburban train covers a distance of 120 km in 2 hours at its scheduled speed. On the return journey, due to signal disruptions at exactly 5 platforms encountered, the train incurs a fixed 'delay penalty' of 4 minutes for every platform passed. If the train maintains the exact same average speed between these platforms as it did on the outbound journey, how much total time is required for the entire return trip?
questions.solution:
1. Outbound average speed = 120 km / 2 hrs = 60 km/hr.
2. Return journey distance is also 120 km.
3. Ideal time for return trip at 60 km/hr = 120/60 = 2 hours (120 mins).
4. Delay penalty = 4 minutes per platform * 5 platforms = 20 minutes.
5. Total time = Ideal time + Penalty = 120 mins + 20 mins = 140 mins.

questions.text: A sum of money is invested at a simple interest rate of 5% per annum for the first 2 years. After these 2 years, the rate is increased to 7% per annum for the remaining 3 years. If the total interest earned at the end of 5 years is Rs 1550, what was the original principal amount?
questions.solution:
Let principal = P.
Interest for first 2 years = P×5%×2 = 0.10P.
Interest for next 3 years = P×7%×3 = 0.21P.
Total interest = 0.10P + 0.21P = 0.31P.
Given total interest = Rs 1550 → 0.31P = 1550.
P = 1550 ÷ 0.31 = 1550 × 100 ÷ 31 = 155000 ÷ 31 = 5000.
Thus the principal is Rs 5,000.

questions.text: Machine A produces 120 units in 4 hrs, Machine B 150 units in 5 hrs and Machine C 180 units in 6 hrs. Each machine works continuously for 2 hrs and then undergoes a 30‑minute maintenance break, after which it resumes the same pattern. All three machines start together at 9:00 AM. When will the total cumulative production first reach or exceed 1000 units?
questions.solution:
1. Rate of each machine: A=120/4=30 u/h, B=150/5=30 u/h, C=180/6=30 u/h. Combined rate when all run =90 u/h.
2. In each 2 h working period all three work, then a 0.5 h joint break. Production per full cycle (2 h work + 0.5 h break) =90 u/h × 2 h =180 units.
3. Number of complete cycles needed: 1000 ÷ 180 =5 remainder 100. So 5 full cycles give 900 units.
4. Time for 5 cycles =5 × 2.5 h =12.5 h.
5. After the 5th break all machines are idle; they start working together again.
6. Remaining 100 units at 90 u/h need 100/90 h =1.111… h =1 h 6 min 40 s.
7. Total time =12.5 h +1.111… h =13.611… h =13 h 36 min 40 s.
8. Starting from 9:00 AM, add 13 h 36 min 40 s → 10:36 PM (approximately 10:36 PM).

questions.text: Let $f(x) = x^3 - 6x^2 + 9x + 1$. In which interval is the function strictly increasing?
questions.solution: The derivative $f'(x) = 3x^2 - 12x + 9$ factors to $3(x-1)(x-3)$. The function increases where $f'(x) > 0$, which occurs for $x < 1$ and $x > 3$. Among the given intervals, only $(3, ∞)$ lies entirely within the region where the function is increasing.

questions.text: A retailer marks up a commodity by 25% above its cost price. He then offers a discount of x% on this marked price. If the final selling price equals the original cost price plus half of the initial profit he would have made had there been no discount, what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
Let Cost Price (CP) = Rs. 100.
Initial Profit (if no discount) = Marked Price - CP = 125 - 100 = 25.
Half of this initial profit = 25 / 2 = 12.5.
Target Selling Price = CP + Half Initial Profit = 100 + 12.5 = 112.5.
Marked Price (MP) = 125.
Discount Amount = MP - SP = 125 - 112.5 = 12.5.
Discount Percentage (x) = (Discount / MP) * 100 = (12.5 / 125) * 100 = 10%.

questions.text: Machine A can produce 120 widgets in 8 hours. Machine B produces 30 % more widgets per hour than Machine A. Both machines work together for 5 hours and then Machine B breaks down. The remaining Machine A continues working alone until a total of 1500 widgets are produced. What is the total time (in hours) taken to complete the production?
questions.solution:
1. Rate of Machine A = 120/8 = 15 widgets/hr.
2. Rate of Machine B = 15 × 1.30 = 19.5 widgets/hr.
3. Combined rate = 15 + 19.5 = 34.5 widgets/hr.
4. Production in first 5 hrs = 34.5 × 5 = 172.5 widgets.
5. Widgets left = 1500 – 172.5 = 1327.5 widgets.
6. Time for Machine A alone = 1327.5 ÷ 15 = 88.5 hrs.
7. Total time = 5 hrs + 88.5 hrs = 93.5 hrs.

questions.text: A 120‑litre vessel contains milk and water in the ratio 7 : 5. First, 30 litres of the mixture is drawn out and replaced with water. Next, 20 litres of the new mixture is drawn out and replaced with pure milk. What is the final ratio of milk to water in the vessel?
questions.solution:
1. Initial milk = 7/12×120 = 70 L, water = 50 L.
2. Remove 30 L (7:5) → milk left = 70−30×7/12 = 52.5 L, water left = 50−30×5/12 = 37.5 L.
3. Add 30 L water → water = 37.5+30 = 67.5 L (total 120 L).
4. New ratio milk:water = 52.5:67.5 = 7:9.
5. Remove 20 L → milk removed = 20×7/16 = 8.75 L, water removed = 20×9/16 = 11.25 L.
6. Remaining milk = 52.5−8.75 = 43.75 L, water = 67.5−11.25 = 56.25 L.
7. Add 20 L milk → milk = 43.75+20 = 63.75 L, water = 56.25 L.
8. Final ratio = 63.75:56.25 = 17:15.
questions.style: Variable Volume Replacement with Additive Step

questions.text: A contractor secures a job worth Rs 48,000. Three workers A, B and C can complete the whole job alone in 10, 15 and 30 days respectively. They start together and work for 3 days, after which A leaves. B and C finish the remaining work in 4 more days. The daily wage for each worker present is Rs 800. What is the contractor’s profit after paying the wages?
questions.solution:
1. Rates: A=1/10, B=1/15, C=1/30 per day.
2. Combined rate =1/10+1/15+1/30 = (3+2+1)/30 =6/30 =1/5 of work per day.
3. Work done in 3 days =3×1/5 =3/5.
4. Remaining work =1‑3/5 =2/5.
5. B+C rate =1/15+1/30 = (2+1)/30 =3/30 =1/10 per day.
6. Days needed for 2/5 work = (2/5) ÷ (1/10) = (2/5)×10 =4 days (matches statement).
7. Wage cost: first 3 days → 3 workers × Rs800 ×3 = Rs7,200.
   Next 4 days → 2 workers × Rs800 ×4 = Rs6,400.
   Total wage =7,200+6,400 = Rs13,600.
8. Profit = Contract amount – Wage = 48,000 – 13,600 = Rs34,400.

A confectioner sells 'Assorted Box' X (cost ₹220/kg) and 'Premium Box' Y (cost ₹320/kg). To reduce inventory of Y, he mixes 2 kg of X with 1 kg of Y to create 'Box Z'. If Box Z is sold at a 10% profit on its cost price, what is the profit percentage earned on the original cost of the 3 kg ingredients?
questions.solution:
Cost of 2 kg X = 2 x 220 = 440.
Cost of 1 kg Y = 1 x 320 = 320.
Total Cost Price (CP) of 3 kg = 440 + 320 = 760.

Profit = SP - CP = 836 - 760 = 76.
Profit % = (76 / 760) x 100 = 10%.

questions.text: A milk vendor has a 200-litre tank containing milk with 30% fat. Every hour he removes a certain percentage of the mixture and replaces it with milk having 10% fat. In the first hour he removes 20%, in the second hour 25%, and in the third hour 30%. What is the fat percentage in the tank after three hours?
questions.solution:
Initial fat = 30% of 200 = 60 L.
Hour1: Remove 20% (40 L) → fat removed = 12 L; remaining fat = 48 L. Add 40 L of 10% fat → +4 L fat = 52 L (26%).
Hour2: Remove 25% (50 L) of 26% → fat removed = 13 L; remaining fat = 39 L. Add 50 L of 10% → +5 L = 44 L (22%).
Hour3: Remove 30% (60 L) of 22% → fat removed = 13.2 L; remaining fat = 30.8 L. Add 60 L of 10% → +6 L = 36.8 L. Final fat% = 36.8/200 = 18.4%.

questions.text: A large storage tank has two inlet pipes, A and B. Pipe A fills the tank in 20 hours while working alone. Pipe B fills it in 30 hours alone. There is also an outlet pipe C that empties the tank in 45 hours alone. Due to a pressure fluctuation, the flow of water through Outlet C reverses direction and starts acting as an INLET for exactly the first 2 hours. After 2 hours, the flow through C reverses again and acts as an OUTLET for the remaining time until the tank is full. If all three pipes are opened simultaneously at t=0, how long will it take to fill the empty tank completely?
questions.solution: Net rate for first 2 hours (A+B+C as inlet): (1/20 + 1/30 + 1/45) = (9+6+4)/180 = 19/180 per hour. Work done in 2 hrs = 38/180. Remaining work = 142/180. Net rate for remaining time (A+B+C as outlet C): (1/20 + 1/30 - 1/45) = (9+6-4)/180 = 11/180 per hour. Time needed = (142/180) / (11/180) = 142/11 ≈ 12.9 hours. Total time = 2 + 12.9 = 14.9 hours ≈ 15 hours.
questions.topic: Time, Work & Pipes (Simultaneous Filling and Emptying)

questions.text: A train covers a distance of 480 km at a uniform speed. If the train had traveled 12 km/hr faster, it would have taken 4 hours less for the same journey. However, in reality, due to mechanical issues, the train stopped for 'x' minutes for every 'y' kilometers traveled, where x/y = 1/30 (i.e., 1 minute per 30 km). If the effective speed reduced by 25% because of these stops, what was the original scheduled time of the journey in hours?
questions.solution:
1. Let original speed be v km/hr. New speed = v+12. Time diff equation: 480/v - 480/(v+12) = 4.
2. Solving gives v=60 km/hr (original speed) and new speed=72 km/hr.
3. Original scheduled time = Distance/Speed = 480/60 = 8 hours.
4. The problem states effective speed is reduced by 25% due to stops, making actual time longer, but the question asks for the 'original scheduled time' based on the uniform speed scenario described in the first half.

questions.text: In a government office, there are 5 files of 'Pending Cases' and 3 files of 'Closed Cases'. A junior officer must select exactly two files for review. P(Case 1 is P) * P(Case 2 is P | Case 1 is P) = Probability of two P.
The rule states: If 1st is P, 2nd MUST be C.
Therefore, given 1st is P, probability 2nd is P is 0.
Total probability of (P then P) = P(P1)*0 = 0.

A and B together can complete a task in 10 days. They work together for 4 days, after which A leaves. B finishes the remaining work in 12 days. If A's efficiency were 25% higher, how many days would A alone take to complete the entire task?
questions.solution:
Let total work = 1 unit.
Combined rate of A and B = 1/10 per day.
Work done in 4 days = 4/10 = 2/5; remaining = 3/5.
B's rate = (3/5) / 12 = 1/20 per day → B alone = 20 days.
A's rate = 1/10 - 1/20 = 1/20 per day → A alone = 20 days.
With 25% higher efficiency, A's new rate = 1.25 × 1/20 = 1/16 per day.
Time for A alone at new rate = 16 days.

questions.text: A retailer purchases 120 units of a gadget at Rs 45 each. He sells 30 units at a 20% profit and 50 units at a 10% loss. The remaining units are sold at a single uniform price so that his overall profit on the whole purchase is exactly 8%. What is the selling price per unit of the remaining units?
questions.solution:
1. Total cost =120×45=Rs 5400.
2. Desired overall profit =8% ⇒ required total revenue =5400×1.08=Rs 5832.
3. Revenue from first 30 units (20% profit): cost 30×45=1350; revenue=1350×1.20=Rs 1620.
4. Revenue from next 50 units (10% loss): cost 50×45=2250; revenue=2250×0.90=Rs 2025.
5. Let price of each of the remaining 40 units be p. Then revenue from them =40p.
6. Total revenue =1620+2025+40p =5832.
7. 40p =5832−3645 =2187 ⇒ p =2187/40 = Rs 54.675.
8. Hence the uniform selling price of the remaining units is Rs 54.675 per unit.

questions.text: A vendor purchases 120 kg of mangoes at Rs 30 per kg. He immediately sells 40 kg at Rs 45 per kg. He then buys an additional 50 kg of mangoes at Rs 28 per kg. The remaining mangoes are sold in two batches: 70 kg at Rs 42 per kg and the rest at Rs 38 per kg. What is the overall profit percentage (to one decimal place) on his total expenditure?
questions.solution:

2. Revenue from first sale =40×45=Rs 1800.
3. Additional purchase cost =50×28=Rs 1400; total cost=3600+1400=Rs 5000.
4. Revenue from second batch =70×42=Rs 2940.
5. Remaining mangoes =130‑70=60 kg; revenue =60×38=Rs 2280.
6. Total revenue =1800+2940+2280=Rs 7020.
7. Profit =7020‑5000=Rs 2020.
8. Profit % =2020/5000×100=40.4%.

questions.text: A retailer sells a gadget at Rs 60 per unit. A bulk buyer purchases 120 units. The retailer offers a 10% discount on the total bill if the buyer purchases at least 100 units. Moreover, if the amount payable after this discount exceeds Rs 5,000, the retailer gives an additional cash rebate of Rs 200. What is the final amount the buyer has to pay?
questions.solution:
1. Total price = 120 × 60 = Rs 7,200.
2. Since quantity ≥100, apply 10% discount: 10% of 7,200 = Rs 720.
3. Amount after discount = 7,200 - 720 = Rs 6,480.
4. Because Rs 6,480 > 5,000, give rebate of Rs 200.
5. Final payable = 6,480 - 200 = Rs 6,280.

questions.text: A shopkeeper marks his goods 25% above cost price. He uses a faulty weight of 900 grams for 1 kg and offers a discount of 10% on the marked price. What is his overall profit percentage?
questions.solution:
Let CP per kg = ₹100.
MP = 125 (25% markup).
He sells 900 g as 1 kg at 10% discount → SP for 900 g = 125 × 0.9 = ₹112.5.
Cost of 900 g = ₹90.
Profit = 112.5 – 90 = ₹22.5.
Profit% = (22.5/90)×100 = 25%.

questions.text: A shopkeeper sells a saree at a loss of 20%. If he had sold it for ₹150 more, he would have gained 10%. Find the cost price of the saree.
questions.solution:
Let CP = x.
SP at 20% loss = 0.8x.
SP at 10% gain = 1.1x.
Given 1.1x = 0.8x + 150.

questions.text: A person deposits Rs 10,000 in a bank offering simple interest at 8% per annum for the first 2 years. After 2 years the rate changes to 10% per annum for the next 3 years. At the end of the 2nd year he deposits an additional Rs 5,000. What is the total amount at the end of 5 years?

Amount = 15000+6100 = 21100.

questions.text: A cooperative society's annual budget allocation for a specific project follows a strict policy: every fiscal year, the allocated amount is increased by 20% over the previous year's figure. A common error in solving this is to calculate a 'net' increase of 40% (adding 20+20) over two years or applying simple compound interest without resetting the base correctly. What is the correct amount?
questions.solution: Year 2024-25 = 18,000 * 1.20 = 21,600. Year 2025-26 = 21,600 * 1.20 = 25,920. The distractor Rs. 23,040 comes from calculating a single year's increase on the original base (18000 + 18000*0.2*0.2) or misinterpreting the compounding.

questions.text: A contractor promises to complete a project in 40 days. He employs 60 men. However, due to supply shortages, the work rate of every single man drops by 25% immediately after day 20. If he wants to finish the job exactly on day 40 regardless of this slowdown, how many additional men must he hire at that moment?
questions.solution: Initial plan: 60 men complete work in 40 days. Halfway (day 20), half the total required work is done. Remaining work needs to be done in remaining 20 days. At day 20, efficiency of each man drops by 25% (becomes 75% of original). Let original rate be R. New rate = 0.75R. Effective men count available remains 60, but their total output is 0.75 * 60 * R = 45R equivalent to 45 normal-men-days per day. Remaining work for 20 days with full efficiency would need (Total Work / 2) / 20 days? No. Original plan: Total Work W = 60 men * 40 days * R = 2400 man-days. Half done in 20 days = 1200 man-days. Remaining 1200 man-days must be done in 20 days. Current effective capacity per day with 60 men at 75% efficiency = 60 * 0.75 * R = 45R (where 1R=1 normal man-day). Days needed for current 60 men = 1200 / 45 = 26.67 days. We have only 20 days left. Deficit = 6.67 days worth of work. Required capacity per day = 1200 / 20 = 60R (equivalent to 60 normal men). Current effective capacity is 45R. Need additional 15R. Since each new man adds 0.75R efficiency, let x be number of men. Total capacity = (60 + x) * 0.75R = 60R => 45R + 0.75xR = 60R => 0.75x = 15 => x = 20.
questions.topic: Time, Work and Efficiency with a Twist

questions.text: A retail outlet marks the price of a television at Rs M. It first offers a flat 20% discount on the marked price and then provides an additional cash rebate of Rs 150 on the discounted amount. If a customer pays Rs 1,350 for the TV, what was the original marked price Rs M?

questions.text: A shopkeeper purchases 120 units of a gadget at Rs 45 each. He first marks the price up by 30% on the cost. On the marked price he offers a discount of 12%, and after the discount he gives a cash rebate of Rs 5 per unit. What is the overall percentage profit earned by the shopkeeper?

questions.text:
A financial scheme offers a simple interest rate of $r	ext{	extperthousand}$ per annum for the first $T$ years and switches to a compound interest mechanism (compounded annually) at a rate of $(20-r)	ext{	extperthousand}$ for the subsequent period. A principal amount is invested such that the total interest earned over 12 years exactly equals Rs. 6480.

It is known that if the initial simple interest rate had been increased by 2 units (to $r+2$) and the switching point delayed by 1 year, while maintaining the same final compound rate logic relative to the new switch point, the total interest would remain exactly Rs. 6480.

Given that the principal amount is an integer, find the value of $T$ (the number of years for simple interest).
questions.solution:
1. Let Principal = P. Simple Rate = r%, Compound Rate = (20-r)%.
2. Scenario 1 (Original): SI for T years + CI for (12-T) years = 6480.
3. Scenario 2 (Perturbed): New SI Rate = (r+2)%. New Switch point = (T+1). New Comp Rate = (20 - (r+2))% = (18-r)%.
4. Note the symmetry: The sum of rates in Scen 1 is 20%. In Scen 2, SI rate is r+2 and CI rate is 18-r, sum is also 20%. This suggests a linear approximation or specific integer property where the 'gain' from higher SI rate in Scen 2 balances the 'loss' from lower compounding rate.
5. However, exact equality of interest implies the principal P must cancel out the complex difference between SI and CI accumulation functions, which typically happens when the time periods are small integers or the rates align perfectly to make the non-linear CI term linearize against the change in T.
6. Testing integer values for T (4 to 7) with a standard Principal P=1000 (common exam simplification): 
   - If T=5, SI(5yr @ r) + CI(7yr @ 20-r). 
   - If T=4, SI(4yr @ r+2) + CI(8yr @ 18-r).
   - For the totals to be identical with different rates and times in a linearized exam context often implies P is large or specific integer cancellation occurs. The only integer solution where such 'rate swap' maintains total yield equality for standard banking arithmetic problems usually points to T=5.

questions.text: A dealer sells two types of tea, Grade A (CP: Rs. 200/kg) and Grade B (CP: Rs. 100/kg), at a uniform 20% profit on cost price. A customer buys exactly 10 kg of each grade. The dealer mistakenly mixes the 10 kg of Grade B with the 10 kg of Grade A intended for another customer. To compensate, the dealer decides to sell this 20 kg mixed bag at a price such that his total profit from this specific transaction equals the profit he would have earned had he sold the two 10 kg bags separately as intended. What is the effective profit percentage on the Cost Price of the mixed bag?
questions.solution:
1. CP of Grade A (10 kg) = 10 * 200 = Rs. 2000. Profit = 20% of 2000 = Rs. 400.
2. CP of Grade B (10 kg) = 10 * 100 = Rs. 1000. Profit = 20% of 1000 = Rs. 200.
3. Total intended profit = 400 + 200 = Rs. 600.
4. Total Cost Price of mixed bag = 2000 + 1000 = Rs. 3000.
5. The problem states the total profit from this transaction equals the intended profit (Rs. 600).
6. Effective Profit % = (Total Profit / Total CP) * 100.
7. Effective Profit % = (600 / 3000) * 100 = 20%.
8. The mixing does not change the weighted average profit percentage if the profit rates are identical.

questions.text: A rectangular agricultural field is partitioned into three sections by two perpendicular internal fences (one vertical, one horizontal) that do not meet at the center. Section 1 (bottom-left) contains a pond with area 30 sq meters. Section 2 (top-right) has an area of 75 sq meters. Section 3 (composed of the remaining L-shaped area formed by Sections 4 and 5 in a conceptual grid, but here treated as a single region for crop yield calculation) is where crops are grown. If the total area of the field is 200 sq meters, what is the difference between the sum of the areas of Section 1 and Section 2, and the area of Section 3?
questions.solution:
Let the area of Section 3 be X. The problem states the total field is 200 sq m, which is the sum of all partitioned parts: Area(Section 1) + Area(Section 2) + Area(Section 3) = 200.
Given Area(Sec 1) = 30 and Area(Sec 2) = 75.
So, Sum(Sec 1 & Sec 2) = 30 + 75 = 105 sq m.
Therefore, Area(Sec 3) = 200 - 105 = 95 sq m.
The question asks for the difference between (Sum of Sec 1 & Sec 2) and (Area of Sec 3).
Difference = 105 - 95 = 10 sq meters.

questions.text: A boat travels between two ports, P and Q. On the first trip from P to Q (downstream), the current speed is 5 km/h, and the boat's speed in still water is V km/h. On the return trip from Q to P (upstream), the current speed increases to 6 km/h, but the distance between the ports remains unchanged. If the time taken for the downstream trip equals the time taken for the upstream trip, what is the value of V?
questions.solution: Let V be speed in still water. Downstream Speed = V + 5. Upstream Speed = V - 8. Time ratio Down:Up is 2:3 (since distances are equal). So, (V-8)/(V+5) = 2/3. Cross-multiply: 3(V-8) = 2(V+5). 3V - 24 = 2V + 10. V = 34 km/h.

A prudent investor splits a total sum of Rs. 20,000 into two parts. Part A is invested at 6% simple interest per annum, and Part B is invested at 8% simple interest per annum. If the combined annual interest earned from both parts is exactly equal to the simple interest on the entire Rs. 20,000 invested at a blended rate of 7% per annum for one year, what is the amount invested at 6%?
questions.solution:

2. Target Interest (Target Rate) = 7% of 20,000 = Rs. 1,400.
3. Let Part A = x (at 6%) and Part B = 20,000 - x (at 8%).
4. Equation: 0.06x + 0.08(20,000 - x) = 1,400.

questions.text: The area of a triangle with vertices at $(1, 2)$, $(4, 5)$, and $(7, 3)$ is:

The other options result from calculation errors or incorrect coordinate substitutions.

questions.text: A tea vendor mixes 10 kg of Type A tea costing Rs 150 per kg with an unknown quantity of Type B tea costing Rs 90 per kg. The resulting blend sells for Rs 120 per kg. He then sells 8 kg of this blend and adds more Type B tea to the remaining mixture, after which the new blend sells for Rs 108 per kg. How many kilograms of Type B tea were used in the initial mixing?
questions.solution:
Let x kg be the initial amount of Type B.
Cost equation: (10×150 + x×90)/(10+x)=120
=>1500+90x = 1200+120x
=>300 = 30x ⇒ x = 10 kg.
Total weight =20 kg, total cost =1500+900=2400 Rs.
After selling 8 kg (cost 8×120=960 Rs), remaining weight =12 kg, cost =2400‑960=1440 Rs.
Add y kg of Type B (cost 90y) and new price becomes 108 Rs/kg:
(1440+90y)/(12+y)=108
=>1440+90y = 1296+108y
=>144 = 18y ⇒ y = 8 kg (consistent, confirming the data).
Thus the initial amount of Type B was 10 kg.

questions.text: A car covers a distance of 120 km at a speed of 60 km/h. If the speed is increased by 20%, by what percentage does the travel time decrease?
questions.solution: Original time = 120/60 = 2 h. New speed = 60 × 1.20 = 72 km/h. New time = 120/72 = 5/3 h. Decrease = 2 − 5/3 = 1/3 h. % decrease = (1/3 ÷ 2) × 100 = 100/6 = 16 2/3%.
